title: Evidence
description: A record of something observed, attached to the assertion it bears on. Cross-cutting rather than owned by a stage (#25), so it carries no x-stage. Consumes #82's primitives and introduces none. ⚠️ Evidence does NOT carry a verdict or a confidence rung — it carries what was observed, and #96's derivation reads those observations. An evidence record that already knew the answer would make the derivation decorative.

allOf.$comment: Kind determines what must be present. Nested inside allOf per #82 — a top-level `if` beside allOf:[$ref] drops the envelope's evaluated-property annotations.

then.$comment: An experiment with no environment cannot be judged applicable to anything, which is what #96's filtering step needs above all else.

else.$comment: A source-based record must say where it came from, or it is an opinion with a citation field.

kind.description: Where the observation came from. `source`: authoritative documentation or published material. `experiment`: something was executed and observed. These reach different confidence rungs (#42) and are filtered for applicability differently (#96), so the distinction is structural rather than descriptive.

summary.description: What was observed, in one or two lines. Human orientation; the derivation does not read it.

sources.description: Where a `source` record came from. Structured because REQ-0004 requires a claim taken from a source to record that source, and a URL inside prose is not a record of anything.

environment.description: What the experiment ran in. REQ-0006 requires this in enough detail to judge whether it resembles the target, and #96's applicability filter is what does that judging. Free-form keys on purpose: the dimensions that matter differ per claim, and a fixed list would be wrong for most of them.

tier.description: #56's sandbox tier. Caps the reachable rung (see 'Which tier can reach which rung').

facts.description: Observed environment facts — os, kernel, interpreter, image, instance type, whatever the claim turns on. Compared against the assertion's targetEnvironment to decide applicability and environment match.

outcome.description: What happened when it ran. ⚠️ NOT a verdict on the assertion — a successful run can refute a claim, and a failed run can support one. Which way it bears is `assertion.supportedBy` / `refutedBy` (#82's naming rule), not this field.

observedAt.description: When the observation was made. Load-bearing for #96's applicability filter, which is the only reason it is required on an experiment.

capture.description: The raw capture — commands, output, logs. #86 in force: this artifact does not re-model a transcript, it points at one.

supersededBy.description: A later evidence record that replaces this one — a re-run, or a corrected observation. Read by #96's applicability filter: superseded evidence is not applicable, which is how a stale record stops manufacturing a contradiction.

tags.description: Changing tags never invalidates an approval (#103) — the clear advisory case, declared rather than inferred.

x-crossCutting.description: #25: validation is cross-cutting, not a tenth stage. Evidence is therefore produced by validation whenever a load-bearing assertion needs it, and no stage in stages/ claims it. That is why there is no x-stage here, and why #90's agreement check passes with none.
